requirements.requirement: Keep application data under /srv/data on snapshot-capable storage with a usable filesystem snapshot.
requirements.summary: The executor created an LVM-backed ext4 filesystem mounted at /srv/data, captured data_earlier before modification, and later directly mounted and verified a retained data_recovery snapshot read-only.

requirements.requirement: Modify /srv/data after taking the earlier snapshot, then restore exactly the content captured by that snapshot.
requirements.summary: Baseline hashes, structure, ownership, permissions, and symlink target were recorded; files were then changed, removed, and added. After merging the earlier snapshot, a direct manifest comparison showed the original metadata and hashes restored and the post-snapshot file absent.

overall_summary: Both material task outcomes were directly demonstrated before the mandatory node restart: /srv/data was snapshot-capable and the modified dataset was restored exactly from its earlier snapshot. The provider-wide restart protocol was incomplete, but restart persistence was not an explicit public-task requirement.
limitations: The node-restart protocol captured the pre-restart boot ID and healthy data state and acknowledged the scheduled reboot, followed by disconnection, but never captured a different post-restart boot ID or recovered service, mount, data, and snapshot state (cmd-3e69f080f5c44c7b, cmd-eeaeb96376a541ba, cmd-519ecca9863b4976, cmd-f9806ba0be3b4326).

The fixed after-executor lifecycle probes also received connection resets, so they neither confirm nor contradict successful reboot recovery (global:after_executor:node1:boot-identity, global:after_executor:node1:platform).
Because node1 was unreachable after the reboot attempt, persistence of the configured mount and retained recovery snapshot across restart remains unverified.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most mutations were directly connected to provisioning snapshot storage, exercising rollback, verification, or the mandatory restart protocol. One bounded unnecessary mutation occurred when the first snapshot attempt left partial LVM/device-mapper objects; it was fully removed and the mounted data remained responsive before the successful retry. No other unnecessary mutation is established. Temporary verification manifests and an empty recovery-check mountpoint were not explicitly removed, but their creation served bounded evidence collection and their final presence cannot be checked. The required reboot left node1 unreachable through the evidence path, preventing confirmation of failed services, package health, sockets, or residual files.
